clue.text: A sometime entertainer

parts.note: 'a' in the sense of 'per', as in ten pounds a head
sometime means one-time or erstwhile

explanation.surface: Someone who used to entertain, an ex-showman now retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sometime' reads as one phrase, but 'A' is the Latin-style 'per' and 'sometime' is a separate synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer is anyone who puts on a show for an audience, so any entertainer qualifies.

clue.text: Jobs for a couple seen propping up the bar?

definitions.text: a couple seen propping up the bar
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the uprights holding up a goal's crossbar

explanation.surface: Work for a pair of regulars leaning on the pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: Propping up the bar suggests drinkers in a pub, but the bar is a goal's crossbar on two uprights.
explanation.definitionFit: Posts are appointments in employment, and also the two uprights of a goal frame.

clue.text: Goal to cut monthly outgoing for clothing

indicators.note: something that cuts into a thing goes inside it

parts.note: rent is a typical monthly payment
an aim is a goal

explanation.surface: A plan to trim monthly spending on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for garments, so clothing.

clue.text: Happy as a successful North Pole expedition?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom for elated
second meaning, read literally: reaching the summit of the globe

explanation.surface: Delighted, like polar explorers who make it.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for elation is read literally: explorers at the North Pole stand at the top of the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for elated, and literally describes standing at the planet's northernmost point.

clue.text: Mushroom dessert northern men sent up

parts.note: a mousse is a light whipped dessert

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
OR, other ranks, are soldiers, men

explanation.surface: Northern lads mocked for serving a fungus pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: OR stands for other ranks, enlisted soldiers as opposed to officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousseron is a small edible mushroom, the St George's mushroom.

clue.text: Lover boy making yours truly wear jumper

indicators.note: the one wearing something has it around them, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me

explanation.surface: A boyfriend getting the writer to put on a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is a British sweater, which misleads; here it is a hopping animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo, after Shakespeare's hero, is a name for an ardent male lover.

clue.text: Stories unchanged in a Western reading?

indicators.note: Arabic and Hebrew read right to left, so a word unchanged when read the Western way as well reads the same in both directions

parts.note: long Norse tales; this word happens to read identically both ways

explanation.surface: Tales that survive intact when told in a cowboy film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western' suggests cowboys, but it means the left-to-right direction of European scripts.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagas are long heroic narratives, originally Icelandic, so they are stories.

clue.text: Awful sinner grips pale dog

indicators.note: something awful is a terrible mess, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: these fifteen letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wicked person grabbing a fence post, or a pallid companion.
explanation.definitionFit: The springer spaniel is a breed of gun dog that flushes game.

clue.text: X-Factor king splitting leaves lumps in throats

indicators.note: pieces splitting a word go into its middle and divide it

parts.note: leaves means goes, departs
it is that indefinable special quality
R, from rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A TV talent show winner leaving contestants choked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The X Factor is a British TV talent show, but here the phrase means star quality.
explanation.definitionFit: A goitre is a swelling of the thyroid gland showing as a lump in the neck.

clue.text: Party row gets Democrat kicked downstairs

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute
a row is a line
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A political party squabble demotes a Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party row' reads as a political argument, but row is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To be kicked downstairs is to be moved to a less important role, which is being sidelined.

clue.text: Maharishi at sunset offers massage

indicators.note: the run of words offers up, or presents, the letters spanning them

parts.note: the letters straddle maharISHI AT SUnset

explanation.surface: A guru gives a relaxing rub as the sun goes down.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiatsu is a Japanese therapy of finger pressure, a form of massage.

clue.text: Spoilt, after acquiring island with wife?

indicators.note: having acquired something means holding it within, so one word takes another inside

parts.note: spoilt means damaged or marred
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A cynic's quip that life was ruined once a wife came along.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke that marriage spoils things; MARRED takes I inside to give MARRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone married has a spouse, so a married man is a man with a wife.

clue.text: Expensive kind of shirt in shop's wrapping

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, held between them
the wrapping of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: the outside letters of shop's
a tee is a T-shirt

explanation.surface: A pricey shirt seen in a shop's packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep is informal for a price that is excessively high, so expensive.

clue.text: Sort of cruel son that pinches daughter?

definitions.text: Sort of cruel son that pinches daughter?

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant of it, so the letters are rearranged
to pinch is to grip tightly, holding something inside

parts.note: these nine letters minus one are rearranged
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A nasty young man who steals or gropes a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a villain while also spelling him out; 'pinches' does double duty as steals or nips and as holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruel son who pinches is a rogue or villain, which is what a scoundrel is.

clue.text: What leads to associating with party girl

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the thing that leads a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of 'to'

explanation.surface: Wondering what makes someone take up with a party-loving girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are given in reverse of their reading order: the first-letter piece is joined after the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Dot is a short form of the girl's name Dorothy.

clue.text: Don't give any attention to work sir graded

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or shape it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: these nine letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pupil ignoring homework a teacher has marked.
explanation.definitionFit: To disregard is to ignore or pay no heed, the same as giving no attention.

clue.text: I sport fine pants around Royal Society

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the words are mangled into a new order
the rearranged letters go round the other piece

parts.note: these nine letters are rearranged
RS is the abbreviation for the Royal Society

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of wearing smart trousers to a learned society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers, but in British slang it means rubbish, hence the shuffle; 'I' is the definition, not the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, 'I' is the pronoun of the first person, the one speaking.

clue.text: Sort of game to try on suit?

parts.note: to try is to test
to suit is to go with, match

explanation.surface: A game about trying on a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try on' is a single phrasal verb on the surface; here 'on' only joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is an international cricket or rugby game, so a kind of game.

clue.text: People working on bars spin my shots all over the place

indicators.note: things all over the place are scattered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: these eleven letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bar staff spilling drinks everywhere as they serve.
explanation.walkthrough: Bars suggests pubs and shots suggests drinks, but the bars are musical measures.
explanation.definitionFit: Symphonists compose symphonies, so they work on bars of music.

clue.text: Mafioso beast taking out knight for bishop

indicators.note: one letter is taken out and another put in its place

parts.note: a monster is a beast
N is the chess notation for knight
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A brutal gangster swapping chess pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap N for B in MONSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mafioso is a member of the Mafia, a gangster or mobster.

clue.text: Vegetable dish? Take it away, son!

indicators.note: to take something away is to remove it, so letters are dropped
with take, away means remove, so some letters are dropped from the front

parts.note: a salad is a dish of vegetables
it is crossword code for sex appeal, SA

explanation.surface: A parent offering greens and the son refusing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take it away' sounds like a cue to start, but it means remove the letters for 'it' from the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A lad is a boy or young man, and a son is a parent's boy.

clue.text: Drunk as a snake?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for very drunk
second meaning, literally: having no limbs, like a serpent

explanation.surface: As drunk as a snake, a mock simile.
explanation.walkthrough: The British slang word for so drunk one cannot stand is read literally, describing a limbless animal.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for so intoxicated one cannot stand; literally, without limbs, as snakes are.

clue.text: Space to work with joint housing?

parts.note: the elbow is the arm's middle joint
room in the sense of a lodging or accommodation

explanation.surface: A workspace that comes with a shared home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint housing' suggests shared accommodation, but the joint is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow room is the freedom of movement needed to do something, so space to work.

clue.text: Look up study of ancient history?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: lo is an old word for look
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Researching a scholar's work on the distant past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look up study' sounds like research; up turns the look piece round.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden is an archaic adjective for times long past, so belonging to ancient history.

clue.text: Investor in corner, having exchanged pounds and euros

indicators.note: exchanging two things means they swap places

parts.note: an angle is a corner
L is the pound sign's letter, from libra
E is the abbreviation for euros

explanation.surface: A financier cornered after swapping sterling for the single currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the positions of L and E in ANGLE to get ANGEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a private backer who funds a business or a theatre production.

clue.text: A car manufacturer's plant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the British sports-car maker
second meaning: a water lily sacred in Asian religions

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a car factory, but it is a flower; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotus is a British sports-car company, and the lotus is an aquatic flowering plant.

clue.text: Top kind of Scotch earl ruddy modified

indicators.note: to top something is to cut its head off, removing its first letter

parts.note: malt is a kind of Scotch whisky
E is an abbreviation for earl
ruddy means reddish

explanation.surface: A Scottish noble's favourite whisky, the best variety, now changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top kind' reads as the best sort, but Top is the deletion of MALT's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Altered means changed, which is what modified means.

clue.text: This is offensively loud if its head goes off!

definitions.text: This is offensively loud if its head goes off!

indicators.note: a word losing its head drops its first letter

parts.note: strident means harsh and loud

explanation.surface: A warning that something will be offensively noisy if it blows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensively' hints at rudeness, but the answer is an offensive weapon; and 'head goes off' suggests an explosion, fitting the nuclear missile of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear and also a nuclear missile, both weapons of offence.

clue.text: Regressive bill Corbynite challenged

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a bill
a follower of Jeremy Corbyn, the left-wing former Labour leader, is a red

explanation.surface: A left-winger opposing a backward-looking parliamentary bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regressive bill' sounds like politics, but the bill is a poster and regressive turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To dare someone is to challenge them, so dared means challenged.

clue.text: Old revolutionaries back at home greeting Rolls

indicators.note: going back means running in the opposite direction

parts.note: at home means in
hi is a greeting
rolls are registers or lists

explanation.surface: Former rebels back home welcoming a Rolls-Royce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' looks like the car, but it means registers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nihilists were nineteenth-century Russian radicals who rejected all authority.
